title: CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md vs .cursorrules & .windsurf/rules
description: Compare CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules, .windsurf/rules, .clinerules, copilot-instructions.md, and GEMINI.md: paths, limits, and personal tone.
h1: CLAUDE.md vs. AGENTS.md vs. .cursorrules, Windsurf & Cline: complete matrix.
dek: File locations, size limits, personal communication layers, and single-source setups across all 7 major coding agents.
lede: Many engineering teams use several coding agents at once—Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI. Shared repo rules tell the agent how to build and test the code. A short 10-line personal block tells it how to talk to you, flag uncertainty, and push back on risky ideas. Below is the complete 7-agent map and how to keep one clean source of truth.
answer: Use AGENTS.md as your shared repo rules file across tools (Codex CLI reads up to 32 KiB by default, and Cursor, Cline, and Copilot read it too). Pair it with tool-specific repo files where needed—CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, .cursor/rules/*.mdc for Cursor, .windsurf/rules/*.md for Windsurf, .clinerules/ for Cline, .github/copilot-instructions.md for Copilot, and GEMINI.md for Gemini CLI. Keep your personal tone preferences in your own home-folder config.

sections.h2: How to keep one single source of truth across tools without drift.
sections.html:
Two simple habits prevent conflicting rules across coding agents:

  1. Keep shared repo rules in AGENTS.md: Put build commands, test runners, protected directories, and commit rules in AGENTS.md. Keep CLAUDE.md short with an @AGENTS.md import plus any Claude-specific notes.
  2. Keep personal tone in user-global files: Do not commit personal verbosity or tone preferences to the team repo. Save personal style in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, or a gitignored CLAUDE.local.md.

Starter communication block for personal global coding-agent files (~360 characters):

## Personal Engineering Communication Style - Give root cause, exact file paths, and minimal diff or command first. - Keep prose under 4 sentences unless I ask for architectural walkthroughs. - Never extrapolate test outputs or claim checks passed unless executed after the final edit. - Ask before refactoring unrelated files or changing public APIs.

sections.h2: What to leave out of coding-agent rules files (and the 32 KiB fine print).
sections.html:
• Secrets & credentials: Never put API keys, tokens, or connection strings in instruction files.
  • Rules a linter already enforces: If Prettier, Ruff, or ESLint enforces formatting automatically, delete the prose duplicate so the agent keeps its context budget for architectural constraints.
  • Novel-length docs: OpenAI Codex CLI stops reading AGENTS.md files once the combined chain hits project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB default in ~/.codex/config.toml). Keep root files under 100–250 lines and move file-specific rules into glob files (.cursor/rules/*.mdc, .claude/rules/*.md, .windsurf/rules/*.md).
  • Role-play costumes: Vague persona lines fade quickly; checkable rules like “state assumptions before editing files” persist across long agent loops.

faq.q: Does Cursor read AGENTS.md or only .cursor/rules?
faq.a: Cursor natively uses .cursor/rules/*.mdc (and legacy .cursorrules) for project rules alongside AGENTS.md compatibility in newer agent workflows. Keeping AGENTS.md canonical and referencing or syncing concise Cursor rules prevents drift.

faq.q: Should personal personality instructions be committed into repo AGENTS.md?
faq.a: Keep repo-committed AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md focused on build commands, code style, security constraints, and tests. Place personal communication preferences in global user files (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md) or gitignored CLAUDE.local.md.

faq.q: What happens if AGENTS.md exceeds 32 KiB in Codex CLI?
faq.a: Codex CLI stops loading additional AGENTS.md bytes past project_doc_max_bytes (default 32 KiB), which can silently cut off nested directory rules unless split cleanly or raised intentionally in ~/.codex/config.toml.

faq.q: How do I merge my AgentTune style into an existing CLAUDE.md without deleting repo commands?
faq.a: Use the AgentTune Instruction Converter & Merger: it wraps your communication preferences in labeled HTML comment markers and preserves every existing line outside those markers.
